His saying, the Exalted: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that is bound to fall﴾. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read "saala saa'il" without the hamza. The rest read it with the hamza. Whoever reads with the hamza takes it from the question (su'al). The ba' may be extra (za'ida), and it may mean "'an" (about). Su'al here means du'a' (invocation): a supplicant invoked a punishment, as related from Ibn 'Abbas and others. It is said: "He invoked (da'a) against so-and-so for destruction (bil-waylI), and invoked against him for punishment." It is also said: "I invoked Zayd," meaning I sought his presence. So the meaning is: a seeker sought a punishment for the disbelievers, and it will certainly befall them on the Day of Resurrection. On this reading the ba' is extra, as in His saying: ﴿grows with oil﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 20], and His saying: ﴿shake toward yourself the trunk of the palm tree﴾ [Maryam: 25]. Thus it is emphatic, meaning: a questioner asked for a punishment that is bound to fall.

(For the disbelievers) means "against the disbelievers." This refers to al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, when he said: "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment" [al-Anfal: 32]. So his request was revealed, and he was killed at Badr by being bound and executed (sabran). He and 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt were killed in this manner; no one else was killed by sabr, as said by Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid. (Sabr: binding a person to be killed.)

It is also said that the questioner here is al-Harith ibn al-Nu'man al-Fihri. When news reached him of the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying about 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him): "Whoever I am his mawla, 'Ali is his mawla," he mounted his she-camel, came, and made his mount kneel at al-Abtah. Then he said: "O Muhammad, you commanded us on behalf of Allah to testify that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah, and we accepted it from you. You commanded us to pray five times, and we accepted it from you. You commanded us to give zakat from our wealth, and we accepted it from you. You commanded us to fast Ramadan every year, and we accepted it from you. You commanded us to make Hajj, and we accepted it from you. Then you were not satisfied with this until you preferred your cousin over us! Is this from you or from Allah?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, other than whom there is no god, it is nothing but from Allah." Al-Harith turned away saying: "O Allah, if what Muhammad says is true, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment." By Allah, he had not reached his she-camel before Allah struck him with a stone that fell upon his brain and came out from his rear, killing him. Then this was revealed: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that is bound to fall﴾, and so on.

It is also said that the questioner here is Abu Jahl, and that he was the one who said this; this was reported by al-Rabi'. It is said that it was the saying of a group of the Quraysh disbelievers. It is said that it was Nuh (peace be upon him) who asked for punishment upon the disbelievers. It is said that it was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), meaning he invoked punishment and asked that Allah bring it upon the disbelievers, and it will certainly fall upon them.

The speech extends to His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So be patient with beautiful patience﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 5], meaning: do not be hasty, for it is near.

"So if you ask me about women, I am
a knower of women's ailments, a physician."

meaning, about women. It is said: "We went out seeking news of so-and-so (nas'alu 'an fulan) and about so-and-so (bi-fulan)." So the meaning is: they asked by whom the punishment will fall and for whom it will be. Allah said: "for the disbelievers."

"Those two asked me for divorce when they saw me,
my wealth diminished; you two came to me with a denial."

Al-Murhaq: the one who is overtaken so as to be killed. Al-Usdah, with a damma: a small shirt worn under the garment. It is also permissible that the alif is changed from a waw, according to the dialect of those who say "silt asal," like "khift akhaf." So the lam in "lil-kafirin" is connected to "waqi'." It is said that the lam means "'ala" (upon), and the meaning is: it falls upon the disbelievers. It is related that in the reading of Ubayy it is so. It is said: they are the stairways of the angels, because the angels ascend to heaven, so He described Himself with that. It is said: al-ma'arij are the chambers, meaning He is Lord of chambers, that is, He made chambers in Paradise for His friends. 'Abd Allah read "dhi al-ma'ariyj" with ya'. It is said: ma'rij, mi'raj, ma'arij, and ma'ariyj, like miftah and mafatih. Al-Ma'arij are the degrees, and from it: ﴿and stairways upon which they ascend﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 33].

Ibn Mas'ud and his companions, al-Sulami, and al-Kisa'i read "ya'ruj" with ya', intending the collective, and because of His saying: "Make the angels masculine and do not make them feminine." The rest read it with ta', intending the group. The Spirit is Jibril (peace be upon him), as said by Ibn 'Abbas; its evidence is His saying: ﴿The trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 193]. It is also said: he is another angel of great creation. Abu Salih said: he is a creature of Allah's creation, in the form of humans, yet not human. Qabisah ibn Dhu'ayb said: it is the spirit of the dead person when he is taken. To Him, meaning to the place which is their abode, and it is in heaven, because it is the place of His goodness and honor. It is said: it is like Abraham's saying: ﴿I am going to my Lord﴾ [al-Saffat: 99], meaning to the place He commanded me. It is also said: to Him, meaning to His Throne.

Wahb also said: the distance between the lowest part of the earth and the Throne is a journey of fifty thousand years. This is also the saying of Mujahid. He combined this verse with His saying in Surah al-Sajdah: ﴿in a Day whose measure is a thousand years﴾ [al-Sajdah: 5], and said: "in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years" is from the end of His command from the lowest of the earths to the end of His command from above the heavens, fifty thousand years. As for His saying in (Alif Lam Mim, Tanzil): ﴿in a Day whose measure is a thousand years﴾ [al-Sajdah: 5], He means the descent of the command from the lowest heaven to the earth, and from the earth to the heaven, in one day, which is the measure of a thousand years, because the distance between heaven and earth is a journey of five hundred years. And from Mujahid also, and al-Hakam and 'Ikrimah: it is the duration of the life of this world from the first moment it was created to the last of what remains, fifty thousand years. No one of you knows how much has passed nor how much remains except Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It is said: the intended meaning is the Day of Resurrection, meaning the measure of judgment in it, if a created being were to undertake it, would be fifty thousand years; this was also said by 'Ikrimah, al-Kalbi, and Muhammad ibn Ka'b. He, glorified and exalted, says: and I finish with it in an hour. Al-Hasan said: it is the Day of Resurrection, but the Day of Resurrection has no end, so the intended meaning is the mention of their standing for reckoning; it is in fifty thousand years of worldly years, and then, at that time, the people of both abodes will settle in their abodes. Yaman said: it is the Day of Resurrection, in which there are fifty stations, each station a thousand years. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the Day of Resurrection, which Allah made, for the disbelievers, the measure of fifty thousand years, then they enter the Fire to abide.

I say: this is the best of what has been said about the verse, if Allah wills, by the evidence of what Qasim ibn Asbagh narrated from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years." I said: How long this is! The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, it will be made light for the believer until it is lighter for him than the obligatory prayer he prays in the world."

Al-Nahhas cited, to confirm this view, what Suhayl narrated from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "There is no man who does not pay the zakat of his wealth except that it will be made into a serpent of fire, with which his forehead, his back, and his sides will be branded, on a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years, until Allah judges between the people."

He said: "This indicates that it is the Day of Resurrection." Ibrahim al-Taymi said: "For the believer, that day will be no longer than the time between the noon prayer and the afternoon prayer." Al-Mawardi reported this meaning as a marfu' hadith from Mu'adh, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah will call you to account in the time between the two prayers, and for this reason He named Himself Swift in Reckoning (sari' al-hisab) and the Swiftest of Reckoners (asra' al-hasibin)."

It was also said: rather, the settling of affairs will take half a day, as in His saying, ﴿The companions of the Garden on that day will have the best abode and the finest resting place﴾ [al-Furqan: 24]. [See vol. 13, p. 22.] This is according to the understanding of creatures; otherwise, no affair distracts Him from another. Just as He provides for them in an hour, so He reckons them in an instant. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Your creation and your resurrection are only like that of a single soul﴾ [Luqman: 28]. [See vol. 14, p. 78.]

It is also reported from Ibn Abbas that he was asked about this verse and about His saying, ﴿in a day whose measure is a thousand years﴾ [al-Sajdah: 5]. He said: "They are days which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, named; He knows best how they will be. I dislike saying about them what I do not know."

It was also said: the mention of "fifty thousand years" is a figurative expression, describing the great length of the Resurrection's duration at the place of standing and the hardships people will suffer there. The Arabs describe days of hardship as long and days of joy as short. The poet said:

And a day like the shadow of a spear, its length shortened
By the blood of the wineskin for us and the clashing of the lutes.

[Ibn Barri said: al-Jawhari attributed this verse to Yazid ibn al-Tathriyyah, but the correct attribution is to Shabrumah ibn al-Tufayl. (See Lisan al-Arab, root ṣ-f-q). The ziq is a vessel made of leather; by "the blood of the ziq" he means wine. The mazahir are lutes; "istafaqat al-mazahir" means some of them answered one another.]

It was also said: there is inversion (taqdim and ta'khir) in the sentence, and the meaning is: "A questioner asked about a punishment that will befall the disbelievers, which none can avert from Allah, on a day whose measure is fifty thousand years, when the angels and the Spirit ascend to Him." This statement is the meaning of what we have chosen. And success is from God.

It is said: al-ma'arij are the chambers, meaning He is Lord of chambers, that is, He made chambers in Paradise for His friends. 'Abd Allah read "dhi al-ma'ariyj" with ya'. It is said: ma'rij, mi'raj, ma'arij, and ma'ariyj, like miftah and mafatih. Al-Ma'arij are the degrees, and from it: ﴿and stairways upon which they ascend﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 33].

(The angels and the Spirit ascend) meaning they ascend along the stairways that Allah made for them. Ibn Mas'ud and his companions, al-Sulami, and al-Kisa'i read "ya'ruj" with ya', intending the collective, and because of His saying: "Make the angels masculine and do not make them feminine." The Spirit is Jibril (peace be upon him), as said by Ibn 'Abbas; its evidence is His saying: ﴿The trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 193]. It is also said: he is another angel of great creation. Abu Salih said: he is a creature of Allah's creation, in the form of humans, yet not human. Qabisah ibn Dhu'ayb said: it is the spirit of the dead person when he is taken. To Him, meaning to the place which is their abode, and it is in heaven, because it is the place of His goodness and honor. It is said: it is like Abraham's saying: ﴿I am going to my Lord﴾ [al-Saffat: 99], meaning to the place He commanded me. It is also said: to Him, meaning to His Throne.

(In a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years) Wahb, al-Kalbi, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: meaning the ascent of the angels to the place which is their abode, in a time whose measure for others, if one ascended, would be fifty thousand years. Al-Hasan said: it is the Day of Resurrection, but the Day of Resurrection has no end, so the intended meaning is the mention of their standing for reckoning; it is in fifty thousand years of worldly years, and then, at that time, the people of both abodes will settle in their abodes. Yaman said: it is the Day of Resurrection, in which there are fifty stations, each station a thousand years. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the Day of Resurrection, which Allah made, for the disbelievers, the measure of fifty thousand years, then they enter the Fire to abide.

I say: this is the best of what has been said about the verse, if Allah wills, by the evidence of what Qasim ibn Asbagh narrated from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years." I said: How long this is! The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, it will be made light for the believer until it is lighter for him than the obligatory prayer he prays in the world."

Al-Nahhas cited, to confirm this view, what Suhayl narrated from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "There is no man who does not pay the zakat of his wealth except that it will be made into a serpent of fire, with which his forehead, his back, and his sides will be branded, on a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years, until Allah judges between the people."

He said: "This indicates that it is the Day of Resurrection." Ibrahim al-Taymi said: "For the believer, that day will be no longer than the time between the noon prayer and the afternoon prayer." Al-Mawardi reported this meaning as a marfu' hadith from Mu'adh, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah will call you to account in the time between the two prayers, and for this reason He named Himself Swift in Reckoning (sari' al-hisab) and the Swiftest of Reckoners (asra' al-hasibin)."

It was also said: rather, the settling of affairs will take half a day, as in His saying, ﴿The companions of the Garden on that day will have the best abode and the finest resting place﴾ [al-Furqan: 24]. [See vol. 13, p. 22.] This is according to the understanding of creatures; otherwise, no affair distracts Him from another. Just as He provides for them in an hour, so He reckons them in an instant. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Your creation and your resurrection are only like that of a single soul﴾ [Luqman: 28]. [See vol. 14, p. 78.]

It is also reported from Ibn Abbas that he was asked about this verse and about His saying, ﴿in a day whose measure is a thousand years﴾ [al-Sajdah: 5]. He said: "They are days which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, named; He knows best how they will be. I dislike saying about them what I do not know."

It was also said: the mention of "fifty thousand years" is a figurative expression, describing the great length of the Resurrection's duration at the place of standing and the hardships people will suffer there. The Arabs describe days of hardship as long and days of joy as short. The poet said:

And a day like the shadow of a spear, its length shortened
By the blood of the wineskin for us and the clashing of the lutes.

[Ibn Barri said: al-Jawhari attributed this verse to Yazid ibn al-Tathriyyah, but the correct attribution is to Shabrumah ibn al-Tufayl. (See Lisan al-Arab, root ṣ-f-q). The ziq is a vessel made of leather; by "the blood of the ziq" he means wine. The mazahir are lutes; "istafaqat al-mazahir" means some of them answered one another.]

It was also said: there is inversion (taqdim and ta'khir) in the sentence, and the meaning is: "A questioner asked about a punishment that will befall the disbelievers, which none can avert from Allah, on a day whose measure is fifty thousand years, when the angels and the Spirit ascend to Him." This statement is the meaning of what we have chosen. And success is from God.

It was also said: it is that the one afflicted by the calamity is among the people without being known as such. The meanings are close to one another. **Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 70, verses 8–10:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿On the Day the sky becomes like molten brass﴾. The governing element (al-'amil) in "yawm" (Day) is "waqi'" (occurring). Its implied sense is: the punishment will befall them on the Day. It was also said: "We see it," or "they will be made to see them," or it is a substitute (badal) for "qarib" (near). Al-muhl (molten brass or dregs) is the sediment and residue of oil, according to the saying of Ibn 'Abbas and others. Ibn Mas'ud said: it is what is melted of lead, copper and silver. Mujahid said: "like al-muhl" means like pus from blood and matter. The discussion of it has already passed in Surah "al-Dukhan" and Surah "al-Kahf" [[See vol. 10, p. 394 and vol. 16, p. (149)]].

(﴿And the mountains will be like wool﴾) That is, like dyed wool. "Ihn" is not said of wool unless it is dyed. Al-Hasan said: "And the mountains will be like al-'ihn," which is red wool, and it is the weakest of wool. From this is the saying of Zuhayr:

*As if the fragments of the 'ihn in every station*
*where they have alighted are the grains of al-fana, unbroken.*

[[Al-fana (with a short vowel and its singular being fanah): the buckthorn berry. It was said: it is a tree with a red berry, which when unbroken is used as weights for measuring carats, each berry being one carat. It was also said: it is used for necklaces. His saying "unbroken" means the berry of al-fana is intact, since when it is broken it shows a colour other than red.]]

Al-futat means pieces. Al-'ihn is red wool, and its singular is 'ihnah. It was also said: al-'ihn is multicoloured wool, so the mountains are compared to it in their variegated colours. The meaning is that they become soft after hardness and scatter after being compact. It was also said: the first change of the mountains is that they become heaped sand (mahil), then like fluffed wool, then scattered dust.

[[Al-mahil: that which is loosened at its base so that it collapses from above onto itself.]]

(﴿And no intimate friend will ask after an intimate friend﴾) That is, about his condition, because each person is preoccupied with himself, as Qatadah said. As the Most High said: ﴿For every one of them on that Day there will be a matter that occupies him﴾ [[See vol. 19, p. 222 and p. 84]] ['Abasa: 37]. It was also said: "no intimate friend will ask about an intimate friend," with the preposition omitted and the verb connected directly. The reading of the majority is "yas'alu" with a fatha on the ya. Shayba and al-Bazzi, from 'Asim, read "la yus'alu" with a damma, in the passive form (the subject not named), meaning: no intimate friend will be asked about his intimate friend, nor a relative about his relative; rather, each person will be asked about his own deeds. Its parallel is: ﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned﴾ [[See vol. 19, p. 222 and p. 84]] [al-Muddaththir: 38].

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 70, verse 11–14:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They will be shown to them﴾, that is, they will see them. There is no created being on the Day of Resurrection, from among the jinn and mankind, except that it is right before the eyes of its companion. So a man sees his father, his brother, his relatives and his kinsmen, yet he does not ask them anything nor speak to them, because they are occupied with themselves. Ibn 'Abbas said: they recognize one another for an hour, then they do not recognize one another after that hour. And in some reports: the people of the Resurrection flee from those they know, for fear of their injustices. Ibn 'Abbas also said: ﴿They will be shown to them﴾ means that some of them see others and recognize one another, then some of them flee from others. According to this, the pronoun in ﴿they will be shown to them﴾ refers to the disbelievers, and the mim refers to the relatives. Mujahid said: the meaning is that God shows the believers the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection, so the pronoun in ﴿they will be shown to them﴾ refers to the believers, and the ha' and mim refer to the disbelievers. Ibn Zayd said: the meaning is that God shows the disbelievers in the Fire those who misled them in the world; so the pronoun in ﴿they will be shown to them﴾ refers to the followers, and the ha' and mim refer to the ones who were followed. It has also been said: He shows the wronged person his wrongdoer and the slain person his slayer. It has also been said: the pronoun in ﴿they will be shown to them﴾ refers to the angels, that is, they know the states of the people and drive each group to what befits them. The sentence is complete at His saying: ﴿they will be shown to them﴾. Then He said: (The guilty one would wish) that is, the disbeliever wishes

(that he could ransom himself from the punishment of that Day) meaning from the punishment of Hell, by giving up the dearest of those who were close to him in the world, but he will not be able to do so. Then He mentioned them, saying: (with his children, and his spouse)—his wife,

(and his brother, and his kin) that is, his clan,

(who sheltered him) who would support him, said by Mujahid and Ibn Zayd. Malik said: his mother who raised him; this was related by al-Mawardi, and Ashhab transmitted it from him. Abu 'Ubayda said: al-fasilah is less than the qabilah (tribe). Tha'lab said: they are his nearest fathers. al-Mubarrad said: al-fasilah is a piece of the parts of the body, and it is less than the qabilah; and a man's lineage (itrah) was called his fasilah, by way of likening it to a part of him. The discussion of the qabilah and others has already passed in Surah "al-Hujurat".

Here is an issue: if one endows (habs) for his fasilah or bequeaths to it, then whoever claims a general meaning takes it to mean the clan, and whoever claims a specific meaning takes it to mean the fathers, the nearest first then the next nearest. The first is more common in usage. And God knows best. The meaning of (who sheltered him) is that it gathers him in and secures him from fear, if there is any fear upon him.

(and everyone on earth, all together) that is, and he would wish that by ransoming them he might be ransomed, (then let it rescue him) that is, let that ransom deliver him. So this implied element is necessary, as in His saying: ﴿and indeed it is an act of disobedience﴾ [[see vol. 7 p. 74]], meaning that eating it is an act of disobedience. It has also been said: "yawaddu al-mujrim" (the guilty one would wish) requires an answer introduced by fa', as in His saying: ﴿They wish you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾ [[see p. 230 of this part]] [al-Qalam: 9]. The answer in this verse is "thumma yunjihi" (then let it rescue him), because thumma is one of the particles of conjunction; that is, the guilty one would wish that he could ransom himself, so that the ransom would rescue him.

**Al-Qurtubi's commentary (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 70, verses 15–18:**

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Nay! Indeed it is a blazing Fire, / Stripping away the scalp, / Calling to him who turned his back and withdrew, / And gathered wealth and hoarded it.﴾

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Nay (kalla)﴾. The discussion of *kalla* has already been given, and that it can mean "truly" (*haqqan*) and can mean "no" (*la*) (see vol. 11, p. 147). Here it may carry either meaning. If it means "truly," the sentence is complete before it, meaning: the ransom will save him. If it means "no," the sentence is complete after it, meaning: ransom will not save him from the punishment of Allah. Then He says: ﴿Indeed it is Laza﴾, that is, it is Jahannam (Hell), meaning its fires blaze (*tatalazza*), as in the verse ﴿I have warned you of a Fire that blazes (talaza)﴾ (al-Layl 92:14) (see vol. 20, p. 86). The derivation of *Laza* is from *al-tala??i* (blazing). *Iltiza'* of the fire is its kindling, and *talazzi* of it is its flaming. It is said that its original form was *lazaza*, meaning "as long as it lasts, because of the continuity of its punishment," and one of the two *za'*s was changed to an *alif*, leaving *Laza*. It is also said that it is the second rank among the levels of Hell. It is a feminine proper noun, so it is not declined (*la yanșarif*).

﴿Stripping away the scalp (nazza'atan lil-shawa)﴾: Abu Ja'far, Shaybah, Nafi', 'Asim in the transmission of Abu Bakr from him, al-A'mash, Abu 'Amr, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read *nazza'atun* with *raf'* (nominative). Abu 'Amr transmitted from 'Asim *nazza'atan* with *nasb* (accusative). For the one who reads it in the nominative there are five possibilities:

1. *Laza* is the predicate of *inna*, and *nazza'atun* is nominative by implying *hiya* ("it is"). From this reading, it is good to pause at *Laza*.
2. *Laza* and *nazza'atun* are both predicates of *inna*, as you would say, "Indeed he is a quarrelsome character."
3. *Nazza'atun* is a substitute (*badal*) for *Laza*, and *Laza* is the predicate of *inna*.
4. *Laza* is a substitute for the subject of *inna*, and *nazza'atun* is the predicate of *inna*.
5. The pronoun in *innaha* refers to the matter (*al-qissah*), *Laza* is the subject (*mubtada'*), *nazza'atun* is the predicate of that subject, and the whole clause is the predicate of *inna*. The meaning is: the matter and the report is that Laza is stripping away the scalp.

For the one who reads *nazza'atan* in the accusative, it is good to pause at *Laza* and to put *nazza'atan* in the accusative as a *qat'* (detached qualifier) from *Laza*, since it is indefinite while attached to a definite noun. It may also be accusative as a *hal mu'akkidah* (emphatic circumstantial clause), as in His saying ﴿and it is the truth, confirming (musaddiqan)﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:91) (see vol. 2, p. 29). It may also be accusative in the sense that it is blazing *while* stripping, that is, in the state of stripping the scalp. The element governing it is the sense of blazing (*talazzi*) implied by the context. It may also be a circumstantial clause for the disbelievers, in relation to its report. It may also be accusative as a *qat'*, as you would say, "I passed by Zayd, the intelligent, the virtuous." These are five possibilities for the accusative as well.

*Al-shawa* is the plural of *shawah*, which is the skin of the head. Al-A'sha said:

*"Qutaylah said, 'What is wrong with him? His scalp has been covered with white hair.'"*

Another poet said:

*"You would have been struck by calamities, a blow whose effect on you would be that the scalp of your head is bare, with its white hairs showing."*

*Al-qatir* means the white hair. In *al-Sihah* it says: "*Al-shawa* is the plural of *shawah*, which is the skin of the head." *Al-shawa* also means the two hands, the two feet, and the head of a human being, and everything that is not a fatal spot. It is said: "He shot him and missed (ashwahu)," when he did not hit the fatal spot. Al-Hudhali said:

*"Among words there is one that has no 'shawa,' when its release slips from the tongue."*

He means: among words there is a word that does not wound but kills. Al-A'sha said:

*"Qutaylah said, 'What is wrong with him? His scalp has been covered with white hair.'"*

Abu 'Ubayd said: Abu al-Khattab al-Akhfash recited this to Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala', who said to him: "You have corrupted it! It is *saratuhu*, that is, its sides (nawahih)." [The addition is from *Lisan al-'Arab*.] Abu al-Khattab fell silent, then said to us: "No, it is *sahhaf* (a mistake), it is *shawatuhu*."

*Shawa al-faras* means its legs, because it is said "*abl al-shawa*" (thick-legged), and this cannot be said of the head, because they described horses by having smooth cheeks and *'itq al-wajh*, which is the fineness of the face. *Al-shawa* also means the worthless part of property, and it means a small, easy thing. Thabit al-Bunani and al-Hasan said: "*Nazza'atan lil-shawa*" means "for the noble parts of his face." Abu al-'Aliyah said: "for the beauties of his face." Qatadah said: "for the noble parts of his creation and his extremities." Al-Dahhak said: "It tears away the flesh and the skin from the bone until it leaves nothing of him." Al-Kisa'i said: "They are the joints." Some scholars said: "They are the limbs and the skins." Imru' al-Qays said:

*"Smooth of the knee-joint, thick of the limbs, contracted of the sciatic nerve; for him are two bony protrusions that rise above the flank."* [Notes from the source: *al-shaza* is a bone attached to the forearm, or the splitting of a sinew; "*abl al-shawa*" means thick of hands and feet; *al-shanaj* means the contraction of skin and fingers; *al-nasa* is a vein in the thigh, and a *shanaj al-nasa* horse is one whose sinew is contracted, which is praise for it; *al-hajabat* are the heads of the hip bones; *al-fal* is a dialect form of *al-fa'il*, the flesh on the hip.]

Abu Salih said: "They are the extremities of the two hands and the two feet." The poet said:

*"When you look you know its pride, and its eyes, but you do not know its extremities."*

He means its extremities. Al-Hasan also said: "*Al-shawa* is the top of the head."

﴿Calling to him who turned his back and withdrew﴾: that is, Laza calls out to him who turned his back on obedience to Allah in this world and withdrew from faith. Its calling is that it says: "Come to me, O polytheist! Come to me, O disbeliever!" Ibn 'Abbas said: it calls the disbelievers and the hypocrites by their names in an eloquent tongue: "Come to me, O disbeliever! Come to me, O hypocrite!" It is said: the caller is the guardians of Hell, and their call is attributed to it. It is also said that this is a figure of speech, meaning that the destiny of him who turned his back and withdrew is toward it, so it is as if it were the one calling them. A similar saying is the poet's:

*"And we descended into the two valleys, and my heart called out to the companion, while the mute gnat (al-'adid al-abkam) was calling."* [The word appears corrupted in the manuscripts: in some it reads *al-'adid* with 'ayn and dad, in others *al-fasis* or *al-fadid* or *al-'asis*; the editors could not find the meaning of any of these in lexicons.]

*Al-'Adid al-abkam* is the fly. It does not call, but its buzzing alerted him, so he called to it.

I say: the first opinion is the literal meaning, as previously explained by the verses of the Qur'an and the sound reports. Al-Qushayri said: The calling of Laza is by bringing life into it when it calls, and the extraordinary events of the Hereafter will be many.

﴿And gathered wealth and hoarded it (wa jama'a fa-awka)﴾: that is, he gathered wealth, put it into its container, and withheld from it the right of Allah the Exalted. So he was one who hoarded much and withheld. Al-Hakam said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ukaym did not tie his purse, and he would say: "I heard Allah say: *wa jama'a fa-awka*."

2. *Laza* and *nazza'atun* are both predicates of *inna*, as you would say, "Indeed he is a quarrelsome character."
3. *Nazza'atun* is a substitute (*badal*) for *Laza*, and *Laza* is the predicate of *inna*.
4. *Laza* is a substitute for the subject of *inna*, and *nazza'atun* is the predicate of *inna*.
5. The pronoun in *innaha* refers to the matter (*al-qissah*), *Laza* is the subject (*mubtada'*), *nazza'atun* is the predicate of that subject, and the whole clause is the predicate of *inna*. The meaning is: the matter and the report is that Laza is stripping away the scalp.

For the one who reads *nazza'atan* in the accusative, it is good to pause at *Laza* and to put *nazza'atan* in the accusative as a *qat'* (detached qualifier) from *Laza*, since it is indefinite while attached to a definite noun. It may also be accusative as a *hal mu'akkidah* (emphatic circumstantial clause), as in His saying ﴿and it is the truth, confirming (musaddiqan)﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:91) (see vol. 2, p. 29). The element governing it is the sense of blazing (*talazzi*) implied by the context. It may also be a circumstantial clause for the disbelievers, in relation to its report. It may also be accusative as a *qat'*, as you would say, "I passed by Zayd, the intelligent, the virtuous." These are five possibilities for the accusative as well.

*Al-shawa* is the plural of *shawah*, which is the skin of the head. Al-A'sha said:

*"Qutaylah said, 'What is wrong with him? His scalp has been covered with white hair.'"*

Another poet said:

*"You would have been struck by calamities, a blow whose effect on you would be that the scalp of your head is bare, with its white hairs showing."*

*Al-qatir* means the white hair. In *al-Sihah* it says: "*Al-shawa* is the plural of *shawah*, which is the skin of the head." *Al-shawa* also means the two hands, the two feet, and the head of a human being, and everything that is not a fatal spot. It is said: "He shot him and missed (ashwahu)," when he did not hit the fatal spot. Al-Hudhali said:

*"Among words there is one that has no 'shawa,' when its release slips from the tongue."*

He means: among words there is a word that does not wound but kills. Al-A'sha said:

*"Qutaylah said, 'What is wrong with him? His scalp has been covered with white hair.'"*

He means its extremities. Al-Hasan also said: "*Al-shawa* is the top of the head."

*"And we descended into the two valleys, and my heart called out to the companion, while the mute gnat (al-'adid al-abkam) was calling."* [The word appears corrupted in the manuscripts: in some it reads *al-'adid* with 'ayn and dad, in others *al-fasis* or *al-fadid* or *al-'asis*; the editors could not find the meaning of any of these in lexicons.]

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 70, verses 19–21:

God's words: ﴿Indeed, man was created anxious﴾. He means the disbeliever, according to al-Dahhak. Al-Hal'a (hala', anxiety and greed) in the language is: the most intense greed, the worst and most shameful distress. Qatadah, Mujahid and others said the same. Haliʿa (with kasra) yahla'u, so he is hala' and halu', in the intensive form. The meaning is that he does not endure good or evil without doing what is not fitting regarding both. Ikrimah said: he is the one who is very distressed. Al-Dahhak said: he is the one who is never satisfied. Al-Manu' (the one who withholds) is the one who, when he obtains wealth, withholds from it the right of God, exalted is He. Ibn Kaysan said: God created man loving what pleases and gratifies him, and fleeing from what he dislikes and resents. Then God imposed on him worship through spending what he loves and enduring what he dislikes. Abu Ubaydah said: al-Halu' is the one who, when good touches him, does not give thanks, and when harm touches him, does not endure. This was related by Tha'lab. Tha'lab also said: God has explained al-Halu', and he is the one who, when evil reaches him, shows intense distress, and when good reaches him, he is stingy with it and withholds it from people. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The worst thing a servant can be given is a greedy, anxious stinginess and a cowardice that unsettles." The Arabs say: a she-camel that is hiliwa'a and hiliwa', when she is swift in pace and light. He said:

A swift, light-footed she-camel: when you turn your back to her, she is fast; when you face her, she is hilwa'.

Al-Dhi'lab and al-dhi'lbah mean a swift she-camel. Jazu'an (distressed) and manu'an (withholding) are two descriptive adjectives for halu' (anxious), with the intention that they precede (the conditional particle) "idha" (when). It was also said: it is the predicate of a hidden "kana" (was).

**Al-Qurtubi's commentary (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 70, verses 22–35:**

His words, the Exalted: ﴿Except those who pray﴾ indicate that what precedes it concerns the disbelievers. *Al-insan* (the human being) is a generic noun, as shown by the exception that follows it, as in His words, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss, except those who believe﴾ [al-'Asr: 2–3]. Al-Nakha'i said: "The intended meaning of *al-musallin* (those who pray) is those who perform the prescribed prayer." Ibn Mas'ud said: "Those who pray it at its proper time. As for abandoning it, that is disbelief." It has also been said: they are the Companions. It has also been said: they are the believers in general, for they overcome excessive anxiety through their trust in their Lord and their certainty. ﴿Who are constant in their prayer﴾, meaning, at its appointed times. 'Uqba ibn 'Amir said: "They are those who, when they pray, do not turn right or left." *Al-da'im* means the still, and from this comes the prohibition against urinating in standing water (*al-ma' al-da'im*), i.e., still water. Ibn Jurayj and al-Hasan said: "They are those who frequently perform voluntary prayers."

﴿And those in whose wealth there is a known right﴾ refers to the obligatory zakat. This was said by Qatadah and Ibn Sirin. Mujahid said: "Besides zakat." 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: "The maintenance of kinship ties and carrying the burdens of the helpless." The first view is more sound, because He described the right as *ma'lum* (known), and what is beyond zakat is not fixed; it depends on need, which varies in quantity. ﴿For the beggar and the deprived﴾ has been discussed in *al-Dhariyat* [[See vol. 17, p. 38]].

﴿And those who affirm the Day of Judgment﴾, i.e., the Day of Recompense, which is the Day of Resurrection. The discussion of it has already passed in Surah al-Fatihah.

﴿And those who are fearful of the punishment of their Lord﴾, i.e., those who are afraid.

﴿Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not something to feel safe from﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "For those who associate partners with Him or deny His prophets." It has also been said: no one can feel secure from it; rather, it is obligatory upon everyone to fear it and be apprehensive of it. ﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or what their right hands possess, for they are not blameworthy. But whoever seeks beyond that, it is those who are transgressors﴾ [[See vol. 1, p. 141]] [[See vol. 12, p. 102]]. The discussion of this has passed in Surah *Qad aflaha al-mu'minun*. ﴿And those who are faithful to their trusts and their covenants﴾ has also passed.

﴿And those who stand firm in their testimonies﴾, against whoever they are owed, whether near or far. They stand by them before the judge, and they neither conceal them nor alter them. The discussion of testimony and its rulings has passed in Surah al-Baqarah [[See vol. 3, p. 415]]. Ibn 'Abbas said: "*Bi-shahadatihim* (with their testimonies) means that Allah is One, without partner, and that Muhammad (ﷺ) is His servant and messenger." It was also read *li-amanatihim* (for their trusts), meaning in the sense of monotheism; this is the reading of Ibn Kathir and Ibn Muhaysin. *Al-amanah* is a generic noun, so it includes the trusts of religion, for the religious laws are trusts which Allah has entrusted to His servants. It also includes the trusts of people, such as deposits. All of this has been fully discussed in Surah al-Nisa' [[See vol. 5, p. 255]]. Abbas al-Duri, on the authority of Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub, read *bi-shahadatihim* in the plural. The rest read *bi-shahadatihim* in the singular, since it is a verbal noun that conveys the collective meaning. A verbal noun may be used in the singular even when it is attached to a plural, as in His words, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the most hideous of voices is the braying of donkeys﴾ [[See vol. 14, p. 71]] [Luqman: 19]. Al-Farra' said: "What indicates that it is *bi-shahadatihim* in the singular, meaning monotheism, is His words, the Exalted: ﴿And establish the testimony for Allah﴾ [al-Talaq: 2]."

﴿And those who maintain their prayers﴾. Qatadah said: "Maintaining them means their ablution, bowing, and prostration." Ibn Jurayj said: "It means voluntary prayer." The discussion has passed in Surah *al-Mu'minun* [[See vol. 12, p. 107]]. Constancy (*al-dawam*) is the opposite of guarding (*al-muhafazah*). Their constancy in prayer means that they guard its performance, neither neglecting it nor being distracted from it by any of the distractions. Their guarding of it means that they observe the thorough performance of ablution for it and its appointed times, that they establish its pillars, and that they complete it with its sunnahs and etiquettes, and protect it from being invalidated by approaching sin. Thus constancy relates to the prayers themselves, while guarding relates to their conditions.

﴿Those will be in gardens, honored﴾, i.e., Allah will honor them therein with various kinds of honor.

Al-Nakha'i said: "The intended meaning of *al-musallin* (those who pray) is those who perform the prescribed prayer." Ibn Mas'ud said: "Those who pray it at its proper time. It has also been said: they are the believers in general, for they overcome excessive anxiety through their trust in their Lord and their certainty. ﴿Who are constant in their prayer﴾, meaning, at its appointed times. The first view is more sound, because He described the right as *ma'lum* (known), and what is beyond zakat is not fixed; it depends on need, which varies in quantity. ﴿For the beggar and the deprived﴾ has been discussed in *al-Dhariyat* [[See vol. 17, p. 38]].

It has also been said: no one can feel secure from it; rather, it is obligatory upon everyone to fear it and be apprehensive of it. ﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or what their right hands possess, for they are not blameworthy. **Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 70, verses 36–39:**

Allah's words: ﴿So what is the matter with those who disbelieve, racing toward you﴾. Al-Akhfash said: "Musri'in (hastening)." He said:

*In Mecca are its people, and indeed I see them*
*Hastening (muhti'in) toward him at the sound.*

The meaning is: what is wrong with them that they hasten to you and sit around you, yet do not act upon what you command them? It was also said: that is, what is wrong with them that they are hastening in denying you? It was also said: that is, what is wrong with those who disbelieve that they hasten to listen to you, in order to find fault with you and mock you? 'Atiyya said: *muhti'in* means *mu'rid'in* (turning away). Al-Kalbi said: *nazirin ilayka ta'ajjuban* (looking at you in amazement). Qatadah said: *'amidin* (intending). The meanings are close: what is wrong with them, hastening against you, lowering their necks, constantly gazing at you. That is the gaze of an enemy. It is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal). It was revealed concerning a group of hypocritical mockers who used to attend him (ﷺ) and did not believe in him. *Qibalaka* means *nahwaka* (toward you).

﴿On the right and on the left, in groups (ʿizin)﴾: that is, on the right and left of the Prophet (ﷺ), in circles and groups. *Al-ʿIzin* means groups in scattered formation, as Abu ʿUbaydah said. From this is the hadith of the Prophet (ﷺ) that he went out to his companions and saw them in circles, and said: "What is the matter with you, that I see you in groups (ʿizin)? Will you not line up as the angels line up before their Lord?" They said: "How do the angels line up before their Lord?" He said: "They complete the first rows and close ranks in the row." Muslim and others recorded it.

The poet said:

*You see us with him, while the night is dark,*
*At his doors in circles, in groups (ʿizinan).*

That is, scattered. Al-Ra'i said:

*O Caliph of the Merciful, indeed my tribe,*
*Their chiefs have come to you in groups (ʿizinan).*

That is, scattered. Another said:

*As if the skulls, from the impact of it,*
*Are khanatil (flocks of wild beasts and birds scattered), falling apart in scattered groups (ʿizinan).*

That is, scattered. Another said:

*When they came upon Udaakh, they pushed its pebbles*
*Scattered in groups (ʿizinan).*

Al-Kumayt said:

*We and Jandal, a rebellious one; we left*
*The battalions of Jandal scattered in groups (ʿizinan).*

ʿAntarah said:

*And an opponent whom I left to one who has a protector,*
*Over whom the birds gather like a band of groups (al-ʿizin).*

The singular of *ʿizin* is *ʿizah*, pluralized with the sound plural (waw and nun) so that this serves as a substitute for what was omitted from it. Its original form is *ʿizhah*, which underwent i'lal (morphological weakening) as *sanah* did according to those who took its original form to be *sinhah*. It was also said: its original form is *ʿizwah*, from *ʿazahu yaʿzuhu* when one attributes it to something else. So each group is attributed to the other, and what is omitted is the waw. In *al-Sihah*: "*Al-ʿizah* is a faction of people, the ha' is a substitute for the ya', and the plural is *ʿizan* (on the pattern *fiʿal*), and *ʿizunna* and *ʿuzun* also with a damma, but they did not say *ʿizat* as they said *thibat*." Al-Asma'i said: it is said "*fi al-dar ʿizun*," that is, kinds of people.

﴿On the right and on the left﴾ is connected to *muhti'in*. It is also permissible for it to be connected to *ʿizin*, on the pattern of your saying: "I took it from Zayd."

﴿Does every one of them aspire to be admitted into a Garden of bliss?﴾ The exegetes said: the polytheists would gather around the Prophet (ﷺ) and listen to his speech, then deny him and lie about him, and mock his companions, and say: "If these people enter the Garden, we will surely enter it before them, and if they are given something of it, we will surely be given more than it." So this verse was revealed. It was also said: the mockers were five men. Al-Hasan, Talhah ibn Musarrif and al-A'raj read *an yudkhala* with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the kha' (active voice). Al-Mufaddal related it from ʿAsim. The rest read *an yudkhala* in the passive voice.

﴿No!﴾ They shall not enter it. Then He began and said: ﴿Indeed We created them from that which they know﴾, that is, they know that they were created from a drop of semen, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, just as the rest of their kind were created. So they have no merit by which they deserve the Garden. The Garden is earned only through faith, righteous deeds, and the mercy of Allah the Exalted. It was also said: they used to mock the poor among the Muslims and be arrogant toward them. So He said: ﴿Indeed We created them from that which they know﴾ of filth, so such arrogance is not fitting for them. Qatadah said concerning this verse: "Indeed I created you, O son of Adam, from filth, so fear Allah." It is related that Mutarrif ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir saw al-Muhallab ibn Abi Sufrah strutting in a *mutarraf* (a striped garment) of silk and a silk robe. He said to him: "O servant of Allah, what is this gait that Allah dislikes?" He said: "Do you know me?" He said: "Yes. You were a foul drop, and your end is a foul corpse, and in between you carry filth." Al-Muhallab went on and left his gait. Mahmud al-Warraq versified the words:

*I marvel at one who is proud of his form,*
*When in origin he was a foul drop.*

*And tomorrow, after the beauty of his form,*
*He will become in the grave a foul corpse.*

*And he, in his arrogance and his pride,*
*Carries filth between his two garments.*

Another said:

*Is there in the son of Adam, beyond his head, any dignity?*
*Yet he is afflicted with five filths:*

*A nose that runs, an ear whose smell is foul (sahak)*
*And an eye with discharge, and a mouth that is slobbering.*

*O son of the dust, and food of the dust tomorrow,*
*Restrain yourself, for you are food and drink.*

It was also said: its meaning is "on account of what they know," which is the command and prohibition, the reward and the punishment. Like the saying of the poet, al-A'sha:

*Have you resolved, from the family of Layla, to depart abruptly,*
*And has she gone far, for one with love to be visited?*

That is: on account of Layla.

﴿Does every one of them aspire to be admitted into a Garden of bliss?﴾ The exegetes said: the polytheists would gather around the Prophet (ﷺ) and listen to his speech, then deny him and lie about him, and mock his companions, and say: "If these people enter the Garden, we will surely enter it before them, and if they are given something of it, we will surely be given more than it." So this verse was revealed. It was also said: the mockers were five men. Al-Hasan, Talhah ibn Musarrif and al-A'raj read *an yudkhala* with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the kha' (active voice). Al-Mufaddal related it from ʿAsim. The rest read *an yudkhala* in the passive voice.

﴿No!﴾ They shall not enter it. Then He began and said: ﴿Indeed We created them from that which they know﴾, that is, they know that they were created from a drop of semen, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, just as the rest of their kind were created. So they have no merit by which they deserve the Garden. The Garden is earned only through faith, righteous deeds, and the mercy of Allah the Exalted. It was also said: they used to mock the poor among the Muslims and be arrogant toward them. So He said: ﴿Indeed We created them from that which they know﴾ of filth, so such arrogance is not fitting for them. Qatadah said concerning this verse: "Indeed I created you, O son of Adam, from filth, so fear Allah." He said to him: "O servant of Allah, what is this gait that Allah dislikes?" He said: "Do you know me?" He said: "Yes. You were a foul drop, and your end is a foul corpse, and in between you carry filth." Al-Muhallab went on and left his gait. Mahmud al-Warraq versified the words:

*I marvel at one who is proud of his form,*
*When in origin he was a foul drop.*

*And tomorrow, after the beauty of his form,*
*He will become in the grave a foul corpse.*

*And he, in his arrogance and his pride,*
*Carries filth between his two garments.*

Another said:

*Is there in the son of Adam, beyond his head, any dignity?*
*Yet he is afflicted with five filths:*

*A nose that runs, an ear whose smell is foul (sahak)*
*And an eye with discharge, and a mouth that is slobbering.*

*O son of the dust, and food of the dust tomorrow,*
*Restrain yourself, for you are food and drink.*

It was also said: its meaning is "on account of what they know," which is the command and prohibition, the reward and the punishment. Like the saying of the poet, al-A'sha:

*Have you resolved, from the family of Layla, to depart abruptly,*
*And has she gone far, for one with love to be visited?*

That is: on account of Layla.

*In Mecca are its people, and indeed I see them*
*Hastening (muhti'in) toward him at the sound.*

The meaning is: what is wrong with them that they hasten to you and sit around you, yet do not act upon what you command them? It was also said: that is, what is wrong with them that they are hastening in denying you? The meanings are close: what is wrong with them, hastening against you, lowering their necks, constantly gazing at you. That is the gaze of an enemy. It is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal). It was revealed concerning a group of hypocritical mockers who used to attend him (ﷺ) and did not believe in him. *Qibalaka* means *nahwaka* (toward you).

*At his doors in circles, in groups (ʿizinan).*

That is, scattered. Al-Ra'i said:

*Their chiefs have come to you in groups (ʿizinan).*

That is, scattered. Another said:

*As if the skulls, from the impact of it,*
*Are khanatil (flocks of wild beasts and birds scattered), falling apart in scattered groups (ʿizinan).*

That is, scattered. Another said:

*When they came upon Udaakh, they pushed its pebbles*
*Scattered in groups (ʿizinan).*

*We and Jandal, a rebellious one; we left*
*The battalions of Jandal scattered in groups (ʿizinan).*

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 70, verse 40–41:

Allah's statement: ﴿So I swear not﴾, meaning: I swear. The "fa" (lā) is a redundant particle (ṣila).

(By the Lord of the easts and the wests): these are the risings and settings of the sun. The discussion of them has already passed. Abu Haywa, Ibn Muhaysin and Humayd recited "Bi-Rabbi al-mashariqi wa-al-magharibi" in the singular (ʿalā al-tawḥīd).

(Indeed We are able. To replace them with better than them): he says: We are able to destroy them, to take them away, and to bring in place of them others better than them in virtue, obedience and wealth.

(And We are not to be outdone): that is, nothing escapes Us, and no matter We wish to accomplish overcomes Us.

(And We are not to be outdone): that is, nothing escapes Us, and no matter We wish to accomplish overcomes Us.

This is the commentary on surah 70, verse 42.

It means: leave them to plunge into their falsehood and to play in their worldly life, as a threat. Occupy yourself with what you have been commanded, and let not their polytheism weigh heavily upon you, for they have a day in which they will encounter what they were promised.

Ibn Muhayṣin, Mujahid and Humayd recited it as ﴿حَتَّى يُلَاقُوا يَوْمَهُمُ الَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ﴾ (until they meet their day which they are promised).

This verse is abrogated (mansukhah) by the verse of the sword (āyat al-sayf).

يَوْمَ بَدَلٌ مِنْ يَوْمَهُمُ الَّذِي قَبْلَهُ (yawm is a substitute, badal, for yawmahumu alladhi qablah, "their day which was promised"). وَقِرَاءَةُ الْعَامَّةِ يَخْرُجُونَ بِفَتْحِ الْيَاءِ وَضَمِّ الرَّاءِ عَلَى أَنَّهُ مُسَمَّى الْفَاعِلِ. وَقَرَأَ السُّلَمِيُّ وَالْمُغِيرَةُ وَالْأَعْشَى عَنْ عَاصِمٍ (يُخْرَجُونَ) بِضَمِّ الْيَاءِ وَفَتْحِ الرَّاءِ عَلَى الْفِعْلِ الْمَجْهُولِ. وَالْأَجْدَاثُ: الْقُبُورُ، وَاحِدُهَا جَدَثٌ. وَقَدْ مَضَى فِي سُورَةِ "يس" [[راجع ج ١٥ ص ٤٠ وص ٢٠٧.]]. سِرَاعًا حِينَ يَسْمَعُونَ الصَّيْحَةَ الْآخِرَةَ إِلَى إِجَابَةِ الدَّاعِي، وَهُوَ نَصْبٌ عَلَى الْحَالِ كَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَى نُصُبٍ يُوفِضُونَ. قِرَاءَةُ الْعَامَّةِ بِفَتْحِ النُّونِ وَجَزْمِ الصَّادِ. وَقَرَأَ ابْنُ عَامِرٍ وَحَفْصٌ بِضَمِّ النُّونِ وَالصَّادِ. وَقَرَأَ عَمْرُو بْنُ مَيْمُونٍ وَأَبُو رَجَاءٍ وَغَيْرُهُمَا بِضَمِّ النُّونِ وَإِسْكَانِ الصَّادِ. وَالنُّصْبُ وَالنَّصْبُ لُغَتَانِ مِثْلَ الضُّعْفِ وَالضَّعْفِ. قَالَ الْجَوْهَرِيُّ: وَالنَّصْبُ مَا نُصِبَ فَعُبِدَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ، وَكَذَلِكَ النُّصُبُ بِالضَّمِّ، وَقَدْ يُحَرَّكُ. قَالَ الْأَعْشَى:

وَذَا النُّصُبَ الْمَنْصُوبَ لَا تَنْسُكَنَّهُ ... لِعَافِيَةٍ وَاللَّهَ رَبَّكَ فَاعْبُدَا

(He means "fa-u'budan" but stopped on the alif, as you say "raʾaytu Zaydan".) وَالْجَمْعُ الْأَنْصَابُ. وَقَوْلُهُ: "وَذَا النُّصُبِ" بِمَعْنَى إِيَّاكَ وَذَا النُّصُبِ. وَالنُّصُبُ الشَّرُّ وَالْبَلَاءُ، وَمِنْهُ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ الشَّيْطَانُ بِنُصْبٍ وَعَذَابٍ﴾ [[راجع ج ١٥ ص ٤٠ وص ٢٠٧.]] [ص: ٤١]. وَقَالَ الْأَخْفَشُ وَالْفَرَّاءُ: النُّصُبُ جَمْعُ النَّصْبِ مِثْلَ رَهْنٍ وَرُهُنٍ، وَالْأَنْصَابُ جَمْعُ نُصُبٍ، فَهُوَ جَمْعُ الْجَمْعِ. وَقِيلَ: النَّصْبُ وَالْأَنْصَابُ وَاحِدٌ. وَقِيلَ: النُّصُبُ جَمْعُ نِصَابٍ، وَهُوَ حَجَرٌ أَوْ صَنَمٌ يُذْبَحُ عَلَيْهِ، وَمِنْهُ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَمَا ذُبِحَ عَلَى النُّصُبِ﴾ [[راجع ج ٦ ص ٥٧.]] [المائدة: ٣]. وَقَدْ قِيلَ: نَصْبٌ وَنُصْبٌ وَنُصُبٌ بِمَعْنًى وَاحِدٍ، كَمَا قِيلَ عَمْرٌ وَعُمْرٌ وَعُمُرٌ. ذَكَرَهُ النَّحَّاسُ. قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ: ﴿إِلَى نُصُبٍ﴾ إِلَى غَايَةٍ، وَهِيَ الَّتِي تَنْصِبُ إِلَيْهَا بَصَرَكَ. وَقَالَ الْكَلْبِيُّ: إِلَى شَيْءٍ مَنْصُوبٍ، عَلَمٌ أَوْ رَايَةٌ. وَقَالَ الْحَسَنُ: كَانُوا يَبْتَدِرُونَ إِذَا طَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ إِلَى نُصُبِهِمُ الَّتِي كَانُوا يَعْبُدُونَهَا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ، لَا يَلْوِي أَوَّلُهُمْ عَلَى آخِرِهِمْ.

(يُوفِضُونَ) يُسْرِعُونَ، وَالْإِيفَاضُ الْإِسْرَاعُ. قَالَ الشَّاعِرُ:

فَوَارِسُ ذُبْيَانَ تَحْتَ الْحَدِي ... دِ كَالْجِنِّ يُوفِضْنَ مِنْ عَبْقَرِ

عَبْقَرُ: مَوْضِعٌ تَزْعُمُ الْعَرَبُ أَنَّهُ مِنْ أَرْضِ الْجِنِّ. قَالَ لَبِيدٌ:

كُهُولٌ وَشُبَّانٌ كَجِنَّةِ عَبْقَرِ [[هذا عجز بيت، وصدره:

ومن فاد من إخوانهم وبنيهم]]

وَقَالَ اللَّيْثُ: وَفَضَتِ الْإِبِلُ تَفِضُ وَفْضًا، وَأَوْفَضَهَا صَاحِبُهَا. فَالْإِيفَاضُ مُتَعَدٍّ، وَالَّذِي فِي الْآيَةِ لَازِمٌ. يُقَالُ: وُفِضَ وَأَوْفَضَ وَاسْتَوْفَضَ بِمَعْنَى أَسْرَعَ.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 70, verse 44:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Their eyes downcast﴾, meaning humbled and abased, not lifting them up because of what they expect of the punishment of Allah.

(Their faces will be covered with humiliation) meaning abasement will overcome them. Qatadah said: it is the blackness of the faces. Al-raqahu (the covering, overtaking) means "al-ghashayan" (overtaking), and from it comes "ghulam muraahiq" (a youth approaching puberty) when the wet dream has overtaken him. Raqihahu (with a kasra on the qaf) yarhaquhu raqahan, meaning ghashiyahu (it overtook him), and from it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And neither darkness nor humiliation will cover their faces﴾ [[see vol. 8, p. 330]] [Yunus: 26].

(That is the Day which they were promised) meaning they were promised it in the worldly life, that punishment would be theirs on it. The report is expressed in the past tense because what Allah has promised will certainly come to pass.
